diagnostic_evidence.quote: such that locally uniformly in $L^2(\Omega_\X)$, it holds

issues.failure_explanation: Strong convergence of mollification is not uniform on any fixed L2 ball, and Fréchet differentiability does not change that. For F=I, each fixed smoothing operator leaves unit-norm high-frequency inputs with order-one approximation error. More fundamentally, finitely many sampled values of x_xi are finitely many linear functionals of x; choose opposite perturbations in their common infinite-dimensional kernel. The network receives identical inputs while the identity outputs differ by twice the perturbation, precluding arbitrary uniform accuracy on a fixed-radius ball. Allowing the radius to shrink with epsilon proves only a weaker shrinking-neighborhood statement. The final remark's uniform O(xi^2) claim has the same obstruction because an L2 neighborhood does not have a uniform H2 bound.
